record.original_question: Is there any semigroup conjugacy relation that is not partition-covering, meaning that there exists some partition of some set that cannot be realized as the conjugacy classes of a semigroup for that relation?

evidence.quote: A natural question to ask at this stage is whether there are any semigroup conjugacies that are not partition-covering. Indeed there are.
Since the identity element will always be in its own conjugacy class, ∼u cannot be partition-covering for any set with more than one element.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Background and definitions. A semigroup conjugacy is a function ∼ that assigns to each semigroup S an equivalence relation ∼_S on S, in such a way that ∼ generalizes the usual notion of conjugacy in groups (i.e., when S is a group, ∼_S coincides with the relation a ∼ b iff there exists g in S with b = g^{-1} a g). Many such semigroup-conjugacy relations have been studied in the literature; one example is the relation ∼_u defined on a monoid M by a ∼_u b iff there exists a unit g of M with b = g^{-1} a g.

Given a semigroup conjugacy ∼ and a semigroup S, the ∼-conjugacy classes of S form a partition of S. We say that ∼ is partition-covering if for every nonempty set X and every partition P of X, there exists a semigroup S with underlying set X such that the partition of S into ∼_S-classes is exactly P.

Problem. Does there exist a semigroup conjugacy ∼ that fails to be partition-covering, i.e., such that for some set X there is a partition P of X which cannot be realized as the partition of any semigroup structure on X into ∼-conjugacy classes?
artifact.status_search_result: The question is answered affirmatively: not every semigroup conjugacy is partition-covering. A standard witness is the unit-conjugacy ∼_u on monoids: since the identity element is always a ∼_u-class by itself, no partition of a set with more than one element that fails to single out one point can be realized as the ∼_u-classes of any monoid structure on that set.
